'''Fiona C. Meldrum''' is a British [[scientist]] who is a Professor of [[Inorganic chemistry|Inorganic Chemistry]] at the [[University of Leeds]]<ref name=gs>{{Google scholar id}}</ref> where she works on bio-inspired materials and crystallisation processes.<ref name=epmc>{{EuropePMC|ORCID=0000-0001-9243-8517}}</ref> She won the 2017 [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] Interdisciplinary Prize.<ref name=rscwin/>

== Education ==
Meldrum studied the [[Natural Sciences Tripos]] at the [[University of Cambridge]], graduating in 1989.<ref name=rscwin>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/InterdisciplinaryPrize/2017-winner-meldrum.asp|title=RSC Interdisciplinary Prize 2017 Winner|website=rsc.org|access-date=2019-01-16}}</ref> She joined the [[University of Bath]] for her postgraduate studies, working on bio-inspired systems where she completed her [[PhD]] on [[Nanoscopic scale|nanoscale]] synthesis in 1992.<ref>{{Cite thesis|degree=PhD|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.305061}}|oclc=257967254|url=https://copac.jisc.ac.uk/id/9529701?style=html|website=jisc.ac.uk|title=Nanoscale Synthesis in Organised Organic Assemblies|last=Meldrum|first=Fiona C.|date=1992|publisher=University of Bath|language=en}}{{Dead link|date=April 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

==Career and research==
Meldrum was appointed a [[postdoctoral research]] [[fellow]] at [[Syracuse University]], where she worked on [[nanoparticle]] assembly with [[Janos Fendler]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Fendler|first1=Janos H.|last2=Meldrum|first2=Fiona C.|date=1995|title=The Colloid Chemical Approach to Nanostructured Materials**|journal=Advanced Materials|volume=7|issue=7|pages=607–632|doi=10.1002/adma.19950070703|bibcode=1995AdM.....7..607F |issn=1521-4095}}</ref> Whilst there, she contributed to the book ''Biomimetic Materials Chemistry''.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Biomimetic Materials Chemistry|last=Mann|first=Stephen|date=1995-12-28|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|isbn=9780471185970|language=en}}</ref>

Meldrum was a [[Humboldt Research Award|Humboldt Research Fellow]] at the [[Max Planck Institute for Polymer Research]], working on crystallisation using [[surface plasmon]] spectroscopy with [[Wolfgang Knoll]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://physicalsciences.leeds.ac.uk/staff/202/professor-fiona-meldrum|title=Professor Fiona Meldrum {{!}} School of Chemistry {{!}} University of Leeds|last=Sciences|first=Faculty of Mathematics and Physical|website=physicalsciences.leeds.ac.uk|language=en|access-date=2019-01-16|archive-date=2019-04-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190416171351/https://physicalsciences.leeds.ac.uk/staff/202/professor-fiona-meldrum|url-status=dead}}</ref> She explored chemical deposition of PbS on gold using [[self-assembled monolayer]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Knoll|first1=Wolfgang|last2=Flath|first2=Johannes|last3=Meldrum|first3=Fiona C.|date=1999|title=Chemical deposition of PbS on a series of ω-functionalised self-assembled monolayers|journal=Journal of Materials Chemistry|language=en|volume=9|issue=3|pages=711–723|doi=10.1039/A807100D}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Meldrum|first1=Fiona C.|last2=Flath|first2=Johannes|last3=Knoll|first3=Wolfgang|date=1997-04-01|title=Chemical Deposition of PbS on Self-Assembled Monolayers of 16-Mercaptohexadecanoic Acid|journal=Langmuir|volume=13|issue=7|pages=2033–2049|doi=10.1021/la9608369|issn=0743-7463}}</ref> Following this position, she worked at the [[Australian National University]] on [[Biomineralization|biomineralisation]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://epsrc.ukri.org/about/people/fionameldrum/|title=Fiona Meldrum - EPSRC|website=epsrc.ukri.org|access-date=2019-01-16}}</ref>

Meldrum joined [[Queen Mary University of London]] as a [[lecturer]] in 1998.<ref name=":1" /> She moved to the [[University of Bristol]] in 2003, where she established new techniques to control crystal morphologies.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Meldrum|first1=Fiona C.|last2=Cölfen|first2=Helmut|date=2008-11-12|title=Controlling Mineral Morphologies and Structures in Biological and Synthetic Systems|journal=Chemical Reviews|volume=108|issue=11|pages=4332–4432|doi=10.1021/cr8002856|pmid=19006397|issn=0009-2665}}</ref> In 2009 Meldrum was appointed as a Professor at the [[University of Leeds]].<ref name=":0" />

Meldrum was awarded an [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council]] Fellowship in 2010.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://gow.epsrc.ukri.org/NGBOViewGrant.aspx?GrantRef=EP/H005374/1|title=Crystallisation in Confinement - A Biological Perspective|author=Anon|website=epsrc.ukri.org|language=en|access-date=2019-01-16}}</ref> Her fellowship considers confined crystallisation in biological systems.<ref name=":2" /> She studied the crystallisation of [[calcium carbonate]] and [[calcium phosphate]] and their behaviour in confined systems.<ref name=":2" /> She demonstrated that confinement slows crystallisation, stabilising [[metaphase]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Wang|first1=Yunwei|last2=Zeng|first2=Muling|last3=Meldrum|first3=Fiona C.|last4=Christenson|first4=Hugo K.|date=2017|title=Using Confinement To Study the Crystallization Pathway of Calcium Carbonate|journal=Crystal Growth & Design|volume=17|issue=12|pages=6787–6792|doi=10.1021/acs.cgd.7b01359|bibcode=2017CrGrD..17.6787W |issn=1528-7483}}</ref> Confined crystallisation can be used to control the polycrystalline structure of crystals. Supported by the [[Leverhulme Trust]], Meldrum showed that even nanoscale confinement can template crystallisation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/research-project-grants/understanding-confinement-effects-crystallisation-using-imaging-approach|title=Understanding confinement effects on crystallisation using an imaging approach |publisher= The Leverhulme Trust|website=leverhulme.ac.uk|access-date=2019-01-16}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/research-project-grants-2017|title=Research Project Grants 2017|publisher= The Leverhulme Trust|website=leverhulme.ac.uk|access-date=2019-01-16}}</ref>  Meldrum looks to use biology to guide crystal growth, demonstrating precipitation with mould and via an amorphous precursor phase.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Meldrum|first1=Fiona C.|last2=Kulak|first2=Alex N.|last3=Yue|first3=Wenbo|date=2006|title=Growth of single crystals in structured templates|journal=Journal of Materials Chemistry|language=en|volume=16|issue=4|pages=408–416|doi=10.1039/B513802G|issn=1364-5501}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title=Calcium carbonate polymorph control using droplet-based microfluidics|journal=Biomicrofluidics|volume=6|issue=2|pages=22001–2200110|doi=10.1063/1.3683162|pmc=3360709|pmid=22655005|year = 2012|last1 = Yashina|first1 = Alexandra|last2=Meldrum|first2=Fiona|last3=Demello|first3=Andrew}}</ref> She also looked how water-soluble block copolymers can influence the crystallisation of [[barium sulfate]] and [[calcium carbonate]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Loste|first1=Eva|last2=Meldrum|first2=Fiona C.|date=2001|title=Control of calcium carbonate morphology by transformation of an amorphous precursor in a constrained volume|journal=Chemical Communications|issue=10|pages=901–902|doi=10.1039/b101563j|issn=1359-7345}}</ref>

Meldrum's work uses nature as an inspiration for materials design.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=http://www1.chem.leeds.ac.uk//FCM/|title=Home Page Materials Chemistry|website=chem.leeds.ac.uk|access-date=2019-01-16}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Wucher|first1=Barbara|last2=Yue|first2=Wenbo|last3=Kulak|first3=Alex N.|last4=Meldrum|first4=Fiona C.|date=2007|title=Designer Crystals: Single Crystals with Complex Morphologies|journal=Chemistry of Materials|volume=19|issue=5|pages=1111–1119|doi=10.1021/cm0620640|issn=0897-4756}}</ref> She focuses on [[Biomineralization|biominerals]] such as bones, teeth and shells.<ref name=":3" /> She monitors the amorphous and precursor phases of biological crystal formation.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=http://www1.chem.leeds.ac.uk//FCM/research-overview|title=Research Overview Materials Chemistry|website=chem.leeds.ac.uk|access-date=2019-01-16}}</ref> Meldrum uses nanoparticles as additives in crystal growth, using the particle surface chemistry to tune particle [[wikt:occlusion|occlusion]]. Amongst several organic additives, Meldrum has incorporated [[amino acid]]s into [[calcite]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hanisch|first1=Andreas|last2=Yang|first2=Pengcheng|last3=Kulak|first3=Alexander N.|last4=Fielding|first4=Lee A.|last5=Meldrum|first5=Fiona C.|last6=Armes|first6=Steven P.|date=2016-01-12|title=Phosphonic Acid-Functionalized Diblock Copolymer Nano-Objects via Polymerization-Induced Self-Assembly: Synthesis, Characterization, and Occlusion into Calcite Crystals|journal=Macromolecules|volume=49|issue=1|pages=192–204|doi=10.1021/acs.macromol.5b02212|bibcode=2016MaMol..49..192H |issn=0024-9297|doi-access=free}}</ref> The choice of additive is guided by genetic algorithms, resulting in the production of crystals with desired properties.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://physicalsciences.leeds.ac.uk/research-opportunity/9/research-degrees/365/bio-inspired-approaches-to-functional-nanocomposites|title=Bio-Inspired Approaches to Functional Nanocomposites|last=Akwei|first=Kimberley|website=physicalsciences.leeds.ac.uk|language=en|access-date=2019-01-16|archive-date=2019-04-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190416185600/https://physicalsciences.leeds.ac.uk/research-opportunity/9/research-degrees/365/bio-inspired-approaches-to-functional-nanocomposites|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Cantaert|first1=Bram|last2=Verch|first2=Andreas|last3=Kim|first3=Yi-Yeoun|last4=Ludwig|first4=Henning|last5=Paunov|first5=Vesselin N.|last6=Kröger|first6=Roland|last7=Meldrum|first7=Fiona C.|date=2013|title=Formation and Structure of Calcium Carbonate Thin Films and Nanofibers Precipitated in the Presence of Poly(Allylamine Hydrochloride) and Magnesium Ions|journal=Chemistry of Materials|volume=25|issue=24|pages=4994–5003|doi=10.1021/cm403497g|issn=0897-4756|pmc=3903342|pmid=24489438}}</ref> She has evaluated how the surface topography impacts ice crystallisation, showing acute geometries give rise to a confined crystalline, which is followed by the formation of a bulk phase.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Christenson|first1=Hugo K.|last2=Meldrum|first2=Fiona C.|last3=Campbell|first3=James M.|date=2016|title=Observing the formation of ice and organic crystals in active sites|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|volume=114|issue=5|language=en|pages=810–815|doi=10.1073/pnas.1617717114|issn=0027-8424|pmid=27994140|pmc=5293020|doi-access=free }}</ref>

The Meldrum group develop [[Microfluidics|microfluidic devices]] to monitor crystallisation processes.<ref name=":4" /> Crystallisation is usually difficult to monitor, as precipitation occurs very rapidly and is severely impacted by impurities. Microfluidic devices offer more control of the crystallisation rate, providing reproducible conditions for crystal growth and the potential to analyse the growth ''in situ''.<ref name=":4" /> Meldrum developed a Crystal Hotel to study crystallisation in a variety of environments and equilibrium conditions.<ref name=":4" /> Meldrum has developed a range of experimental techniques; including [[Bragg's law|Bragg]] coherent diffraction imaging, [[Brewster angle microscope|Brewster angle microscopy]], liquid-cell [[Atomic force microscopy]] (AFM) and [[Infrared spectroscopy]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Meldrum|first1=Fiona C.|last2=Robinson|first2=Ian K.|last3=Ashbrook|first3=Sharon E.|last4=Tang|first4=Chiu C.|last5=Harder|first5=Ross J.|last6=Holden|first6=Mark A.|last7=Kim|first7=Yi-Yeoun|last8=Kanwal|first8=Nasima|last9=Clark|first9=Jesse N.|date=2018|title=Visualization of the effect of additives on the nanostructures of individual bio-inspired calcite crystals|journal=Chemical Science|volume=10|issue=4|pages=1176–1185|language=en|doi=10.1039/C8SC03733G|pmid=30774916|pmc=6349071|issn=2041-6539}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ccp14.ac.uk/ccp/web-mirrors/bristol/section/fcm.htm|title=Dr Fiona Meldrum|website=ccp14.ac.uk|access-date=2019-01-16}}</ref>

===Awards and honours===
Meldrum was appointed lead editor of the [[Materials Research Society]] (MRS) Bulletin in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/BB400E2B6DCE7AD6184AE4A61B04CEE6/S088376941500322Xa.pdf/fiona-meldrum-to-lead-mrs-bulletin-editorial-board.pdf|title=Fiona Meldrum to lead MRS Bulletin Editorial Board|date=2016|website=MRS Bulletin|access-date=2019-01-16}}</ref> In 2017, she was awarded the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] Interdisciplinary Prize.<ref name=rscwin/> She was awarded a [[European Research Council]] (ERC) advanced grant in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elsevier.com/events/conferences/international-colloids-conference/program/speakers2|title=Speakers - 9th International Colloids Conference - Elsevier|website=elsevier.com|access-date=2019-01-16}}</ref>
